Fair-Trade Coffee

Served at: Earth Day

Serves 4-6 (about 48 fl oz / 1.4 L)Prep 5 minutesCook 5 minutes

On Earth Day, celebrating Fair-Trade Coffee is a perfect way to honor our planet and its people. This isn't just about a delicious beverage; it's about making an ethical choice that supports sustainable farming practices, protects ecosystems, and ensures fair wages for coffee growers worldwide. Enjoying a cup of fair-trade coffee is a simple yet powerful act of global responsibility.

Ingredients

  • 8 tablespoons (approx. 45-50 g) whole bean or ground fair-trade coffee
  • 48 fluid ounces (1.4 L) filtered water
  • Optional: Milk, sugar, or other preferred additions

Method

  1. Select high-quality, whole bean or ground fair-trade coffee, ensuring it carries certifications like Fair Trade Certified to guarantee ethical sourcing.
  2. If using whole beans, grind them to a medium-coarse consistency, similar to sea salt, for optimal extraction and flavor.
  3. Heat the filtered water to just off the boil, ideally between 195-205°F (90-96°C), as this temperature range is best for brewing.
  4. Prepare your chosen brewing device (e.g., French press, pour-over, drip machine). If using a pour-over or French press, pre-warm your vessel with a splash of hot water and discard it.
  5. Add the ground coffee to your brewing device. If using a pour-over, place a filter in the cone and rinse it with hot water to remove any paper taste.
  6. Pour a small amount of hot water over the coffee grounds, just enough to saturate them, and let it 'bloom' for 30 seconds. This step allows gases to escape, enhancing flavor.
  7. Slowly pour the remaining hot water over the grounds in a circular motion, ensuring even saturation. For a French press, steep for 4 minutes before gently pressing the plunger.
  8. Once brewed, pour the coffee into your favorite reusable mug or serving carafe, minimizing waste.
  9. Serve immediately, adding milk, sugar, or other desired accompaniments if preferred.

Tips

  • Embrace sustainability by using reusable coffee filters or composting your spent coffee grounds for your garden, enriching the soil naturally.
  • Experiment with different fair-trade coffee origins (e.g., Ethiopian, Colombian, Peruvian) to discover unique flavor profiles and support diverse farming communities.
  • Consider brewing methods like a French press or pour-over, which often require less energy than electric drip machines, further reducing your environmental footprint.
